rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Conspirituality as one road with two doors", "body": "Chance described conspirituality as a word that captured how an honest spiritual path leads into conspiracy, and how conspiracy research eventually leads back to spirituality. He said he went through the film Zeitgeist and an atheist phase before running into what he called pop culture Gnosticism, the prison planet and demiurge idea, which he argued can become an excuse for staying a victim. Chance said he rejected that view and saw at least as much reason to call the world good. One of the hosts described returning to conspiracy research when the pandemic hit."}, {"title": "Despair, balance, and sharing what uplifts", "body": "Chance argued that much of the material circulating in conspiracy circles delivered despair, and he said sharing it did the beast's job for it. He preferred solutions oriented and uplifting content and described a sober festival near his home, which he guessed drew about 1,200 people, as an example of fun without alcohol. One of the hosts said the pair found that arguing left against right during the pandemic led them toward spirituality. Chance encouraged balancing dark topics with uplifting ones while warning against bypassing real corruption."}, {"title": "Pain, illness, and fragmented souls", "body": "Chance said he saw pain and illness as a guidance system rather than a punishment, with a message in every injury and disease, and he tied this to his Biofield Tuning work. He called suppression based medicine a hindrance to finding root causes. He offered a personal theory that people in denial leave behind soul fragments after death, which he described as speculation. Chance also said germ theory had holes, while granting that some bacteria and molds can harm health, and he proposed a consciousness component."}, {"title": "Creativity, imagination, and the inner savior", "body": "Chance said creativity was the most important element of a spiritual path, because aligning with the creator meant becoming more original, and he described making art in his twenties as ending a sense of emptiness. He called the flow state of making it up as you go the closest feeling to being tapped into source. Aaron described quitting his corporate job in 2021 and feeling free. Chance also gave an alchemical reading in which the external savior is the mercury to be removed before the philosopher stone appears."}, {"title": "Quartz, floods, and a ring-shaped world", "body": "Chance described watching glowing orbs while camping during the 2017 eclipse and, citing Dr. Gregory Little, speculated that some sky phenomena might be plasma life forms tied to quartz and the piezoelectric effect. He then discussed George Wiseman's hydrogen machine and its sludge, and used it to wonder whether floods recharge the world like a battery. Chance also floated an ice wall at Antarctica and rings of land with other planets as suns and moons, repeatedly calling it speculation."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Kam and Aaron on the Alt-ernative Podcast for a wide-ranging conversation that moved from conspirituality and creativity to cosmology and common sense.
